title: Resolve a view
starter:
type view =
  | Buffer of int                (* a whole buffer of n elements *)
  | Shrink of view * int * int   (* parent, offset, k elements:  shrink p off shape=[k] *)
  | Elem of view * int           (* parent, offset, one element: shrink p off shape=[] *)

(* resolve v = (start, len): where v starts inside its buffer, and how many elements it covers.
   Raise (Invalid_argument "out of bounds") if any step doesn't fit inside its parent. *)
let rec resolve (v : view) : int * int =
  match v with
  | Buffer n -> (0, n)
  | Shrink (p, off, k) -> let (s, _) = resolve p in (s + off, k)
  | Elem (p, off) -> let (s, _) = resolve p in (s + off, 1)
hints: Each step only knows its parent. Resolve the parent first, then check the new window against the parent's length, not the buffer's.
A step with offset `off` and `k` elements fits when `off >= 0` and `off + k <= parent_len`. An `Elem` is the same check with `k = 1`.
The test `Shrink (Shrink (Buffer 10, 0, 4), 2, 3)` fails only if you compare against the parent's 4 elements. The buffer's 10 elements would wrongly let it through.

answer.code:
type view =
  | Buffer of int                (* a whole buffer of n elements *)
  | Shrink of view * int * int   (* parent, offset, k elements:  shrink p off shape=[k] *)
  | Elem of view * int           (* parent, offset, one element: shrink p off shape=[] *)

let rec resolve (v : view) : int * int =
  let step p off k =
    let (s, len) = resolve p in
    if off < 0 || off + k > len then raise (Invalid_argument "out of bounds");
    (s + off, k) in
  match v with
  | Buffer n -> (0, n)
  | Shrink (p, off, k) -> step p off k
  | Elem (p, off) -> step p off 1
answer.explain: The solution resolves the parent to `(start, len)`, checks `0 <= off` and `off + k <= len` against that parent, and returns `(start + off, k)`. Checking against the parent rather than the whole buffer is what catches a view that fits the buffer but spills out of the view it was cut from.
